election.note: Also scrutin for the act of voting.

general election.note: Used for the UK, Canada, etc. (plural élections générales in headings). France has no exact equivalent; for France use élections législatives, présidentielle, etc.

primary.note: Full form élection primaire. In French press, primaire is also used for party-run selections outside the US.

runoff.note: Used in France, Switzerland and Canada. Scrutin de ballottage is the formal variant in Belgium and Canada.

by-election.note: Standard in France and Canada. Plural élections partielles.

special election.note: Used for the US. In France it is also called élection partielle. Use élection extraordinaire only for Canadian or other legal contexts that specify it.

recall election.note: Alternatives: scrutin révocatoire, vote de révocation. Press often explains the US recall (e.g. California) on first mention.

contest.note: No exact single word in French. For a specific seat, use élection pour le poste de / le siège de…. For a ballot question, use question.

race.note: Informal: course à la mairie, course au Sénat. Not for formal tables, where scrutin or élection is used.

ballot measure.note: Canadian usage. Switzerland uses objet soumis au vote or objet de votation. For US measures, press often uses référendum d'initiative populaire or consultation.

referendum.note: Plural référendums. In Switzerland a popular vote is called votation, and in Belgium consultation populaire.

initiative.note: Swiss and general usage. In France, référendum d'initiative partagée is a distinct mechanism.

proposition.note: US numbered measure, e.g. la proposition 8 (Californie). Keep lowercase in running text.

retention election.note: Descriptive rendering for US judges. Press also uses vote de confirmation des juges. No French equivalent institution.

incumbent.note: Feminine: sortante. Usually with a noun, e.g. député sortant. Titulaire du siège is also used.

nominee.note: Feminine: candidate investie. Also candidat désigné for US nominees.

write-in.note: Descriptive. There is no fixed term. Switzerland uses voix éparses for scattered votes for non-candidates.

unopposed.note: Canada: also élu par acclamation. Switzerland: élection tacite.

ballot.note: Short form bulletin. Distinguish from scrutin, which is the vote itself.

votes cast.note: The count is labelled votants (France). Bulletins déposés is a descriptive alternative. Do not equate with suffrages exprimés, which excludes blank and invalid ballots in France.

valid votes.note: Plural suffrages exprimés in tables. In France it excludes blank and null ballots. Belgium and Switzerland: votes valables or bulletins valables. Canada: votes valides or bulletins valides.

invalid votes.note: Plural bulletins nuls in tables. Canada: bulletins rejetés.

blank votes.note: Plural votes blancs or bulletins blancs. In France, blank votes are counted separately from suffrages exprimés.

turnout.note: Also participation. The abstention rate is the complement (taux d'abstention).

registered voters.note: In tables, the plural label inscrits or électeurs inscrits is used.

electorate.note: The legal term. Électorat is the general or sociological sense.

vote share.note: Also pourcentage des suffrages exprimés. Swiss usage: part des suffrages.

margin.note: Écart en points for the percentage difference. Canada: also marge.

swing.note: Written variation (en points). Swing is used as an anglicism in some press.

majority.note: More than half. Majorité simple is a distinct term, with a meaning that varies by country.

seat.note: Also mandat in some contexts, especially for Germany and Belgium.

constituency.note: Same word for UK constituencies and French or Canadian ridings.

district.note: Used for US districts: district congressionnel. Use circonscription for French or Canadian equivalents.

ward.note: Quebec municipal usage. Quartier is also used. For UK wards, press often keeps ward in italics.

precinct.note: For the US precinct, the smallest reporting unit; plural: bureaux de vote.

polling station.note: Canada: bureau de scrutin. Switzerland: local de vote.

reporting unit.note: Working term. No official French equivalent.

county.note: Used for the US, UK and Ireland. Not a French département.

state.note: Capitalised for federated states. German Länder are called Land (plural Länder) in French.

region.note: Belgium: Région also denotes a federated entity.

polity.note: Descriptive. Also territoire for non-sovereign cases.

jurisdiction.note: In an administrative sense, territoire de compétence or ressort is also used.

boundaries.note: Plural limites, e.g. limites des circonscriptions. Also découpage for the whole delineation.

legislature.note: Législature also means the period of a mandate, or a US state legislature in press.

parliament.note: Capitalised when naming a specific body.

senate.note: Capitalised for specific bodies: le Sénat.

house of representatives.note: US House. Canada's equivalent is Chambre des communes.

mayor.note: Belgium: bourgmestre. Switzerland: syndic in some cantons. Feminine: la maire.

officeholder.note: For elected officials, élu is common. Titulaire d'un mandat for mandates.

term limit.note: Also limitation du nombre de mandats.

independent.note: Feminine: indépendante. France: sans étiquette in election listings.

alliance.note: France: union, e.g. Nouveau Front populaire. Belgium: cartel for joint lists.

party list.note: Also liste de parti. Do not confuse with liste électorale (the electoral roll).

preference vote.note: Belgium: also vote de préférence. Switzerland: panachage and cumul relate to similar options.

leveling seat.note: Translation of Ausgleichsmandat. Also siège de compensation.

threshold.note: Seuil de représentation. Colloquial: barre or clause barrière.

quota.note: For STV in Ireland, quota is also commonly used. Droop quota: quotient de Droop.

first past the post.term: scrutin majoritaire uninominal à un tour
first past the post.note: Often glossed in press as scrutin à un tour.

ranked-choice voting.note: Also scrutin à second tour instantané. Québec press uses vote préférentiel; US press often glosses vote par classement.

mixed-member proportional.note: Canadian term. For Germany: scrutin proportionnel personnalisé or système mixte compensatoire.

D'Hondt method.note: Also méthode de la plus forte moyenne.

seat allocation.note: Attribution des sièges is also used.

transfer.note: Transfert de voix. Report de voix is used for second-round vote movements.

count.note: For STV, décompte also occurs. Dépouillement means counting generally.

official results.note: France: résultats proclamés. Plural in headings.

certified.note: Used for US certification. France: proclamé. Canada: validé.

preliminary results.note: Canada: résultats préliminaires or non officiels. Plural in headings.

election night.note: Nuit électorale is used for long US counts.

called.note: Press: X est donné gagnant / victoire annoncée.

votes counted.note: Plural bulletins dépouillés or suffrages dépouillés.

absentee ballot.note: No fixed single term. US press often says vote par correspondance. Canada: vote par bulletin spécial.

flip.note: Siège basculé: seat that changes party.

gain.note: Siège gagné: seat won from another party.

gerrymander.note: Also charcutage électoral (colloquial). Used as a loanword.

electoral college.note: US body. In France, grands électeurs refers to different electors (senatorial). The electors are called grands électeurs in US coverage.

elector.note: For US electors. In France the term also covers senatorial electors.

convention.note: Convention d'investiture or convention nationale of a party.

roll call.note: At US conventions, appel nominal des États.

shapes.note: Plural contours. Fond de carte or tracé also used.

workbench.note: Atelier de données or atelier d'analyse.
